question: Explain why total formation-volume factor Bt stays identical to Bo below bubble-point pressure even after free gas evolves, using the internal reservoir text.
answer:
The total formation-volume factor $ B_t $ remains identical to $ B_o $ (oil formation-volume factor) below the bubble-point pressure because, under these conditions, no free gas is present in the reservoir fluid. 

Below the bubble-point pressure, the fluid exists as a single phase—pure oil. As a result, the volume of oil required to produce one standard cubic foot of oil (SCF/oil) is the same as the volume of oil itself, since there is no gas to contribute to the total volume. Therefore, the total formation-volume factor $ B_t $, which accounts for the entire volume of the fluid (oil + gas), is equal to $ B_o $, the oil formation-volume factor. 

This equality holds even if free gas evolves from the oil because, below the bubble-point pressure, the gas remains dissolved in the oil and does not exist as a separate phase, so it does not affect the total volume factor.
